about: I am a postdoctoral researcher in the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering at The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST), working with Prof. Zhe Wang.

My research interests lie in Urban Energy System Modeling and Geographic Information System. My work connects geospatial computing with urban building energy modelling, renewable energy systems, and urban energy resilience.

I received my Ph.D. in Civil Engineering from HKUST in 2026. During my doctoral studies, I was a visiting Ph.D. student in Urban Studies and Planning at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. I previously received an M.Eng. from Wuhan University and a B.Sc. from Wuhan University of Technology, both in Geographic Information Science.

news.text: GeoBEM was featured as a highlighted project by the HKUST GREAT Smart Cities Institute (GSCI).
Selected as an honoree in the IBPSA-USA 2026–2027 Simulation Showcase.
Started as a postdoctoral researcher at HKUST, working with Prof. Zhe Wang.
Received the Best Paper Award at the 4th International Conference on Urban Science and Intelligence, Guangzhou.
Received the Best Paper Award at Nexus Forum 2026, Oxford.
Completed my Ph.D. in Civil Engineering at HKUST.
Received the Best Paper Award and Best Oral Presentation Award at BAS2026, Hong Kong.
Completed my visiting Ph.D. research at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT).
Received the Best Student Paper Award at the 9th International Conference on Energy, Electricity and Power Engineering, Nanjing.
Selected as a winner in the IBPSA-USA 2025–2026 Simulation Showcase.

Awarded the 2025–2026 Dissertation Fellowship from the Peking University–Lincoln Institute Center for Urban Development and Land Policy for GIS-empowered Modelling and Analysis for Sustainable Energy Systems and Resilient Cities.
Received the Global Research Award from The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology.
Received the Merit Prize at the 11th Hong Kong University Student Innovation and Entrepreneurship Competition, Hong Kong.
Received the Second Prize at the 7th China Alliance for Heating, Ventilation and Air Conditioning (CAHVAC) Student Competition, Suzhou, China.

team_intro: We are the Urban Group within the Smart Building and Construction Lab at the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST). Our team brings together diverse backgrounds in geographic information science (GIS), architecture, urban planning, and environmental science. Our research spans GIS, urban energy systems, urban sustainability, and resilience, with a shared goal of advancing more sustainable and resilient cities.
